name: TD sequential setup nine with perfection
note: DeMark bar counting and nothing else. A buy setup counts consecutive bars closing below the close `off` bars back; at count `setup_len` the perfection inequality is tested (min of the last two setup lows at or below min of setup bars L-3 and L-2) and, if it fails, the count is allowed to extend to max_len looking for the first bar that satisfies it. Sell setup is the mirror. entry_mode 0 enters at the qualifying close, 1 is DeMark's Method 2 (the first later bar that closes back above close[-off]), 2 runs the Countdown to 13 on close <= low[-2]. The TDST target -- the first close beyond the extreme of the setup bars -- is the family's own exit_signal.
source: Thomas DeMark, 'The New Science of Technical Analysis' (1994). Setup rule (9 consecutive closes with Close[i] < Close[i-4]) and the countdown's switch to a close[2]-based comparison confirmed in the open-source implementation https://github.com/Forte11Cuba/TD-Sequential-Tom-DeMark. Independent backtest with the same 4-bar offset, 9-bar count and 'Method 2' entry, across 42 futures markets 1980-2013: https://oxfordstrat.com/trading-strategies/td-sequential-1/ - note performance deteriorates markedly at $100 round-turn costs, so this needs liquid names and passive fills.
code:
def _setups(c, h, l, off, L, mx, perfect, up):
    """Indices of qualifying setup completions, and the setup's extreme.

    up=False is the buy setup (closes below close[-off]); up=True the sell.
    Returns (done_i, extreme, bars) for every completion, in bar order.
    """
    n = len(c)
    out = []
    cnt = 0
    idx = []
    done = False
    for i in range(off, n):
        hit = (c[i] > c[i - off]) if up else (c[i] < c[i - off])
        if hit:
            cnt += 1
            idx.append(i)
        else:
            cnt = 0
            idx = []
            done = False
            continue
        if done or cnt < L or cnt > mx:
            continue
        ok = True
        if perfect and L >= 4:
            a = idx[cnt - 2]
            b = idx[cnt - 1]
            r1 = idx[L - 4]
            r2 = idx[L - 3]
            if up:
                ok = max(h[a], h[b]) >= max(h[r1], h[r2])
            else:
                ok = min(l[a], l[b]) <= min(l[r1], l[r2])
        if ok:
            done = True
            ext = max(h[j] for j in idx) if not up else min(l[j] for j in idx)
            out.append((i, ext, list(idx)))
    return out


def family_init(ctx):
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    h = [float(b["h"]) for b in bars]
    l = [float(b["l"]) for b in bars]
    off = max(1, int(ctx.p.off))
    L = max(4, int(ctx.p.setup_len))
    mx = max(L, int(ctx.p.max_len))
    pf = int(ctx.p.perfect)
    mode = int(ctx.p.entry_mode)
    cdl = max(1, int(ctx.p.cd_len))
    cdo = max(1, int(ctx.p.cd_off))

    sig = [0.0] * n
    lvl = [None] * n

    for up in (False, True):
        d = -1.0 if up else 1.0
        for done_i, ext, idx in _setups(c, h, l, off, L, mx, pf, up):
            fire = None
            if mode == 0:
                fire = done_i
            elif mode == 1:                       # DeMark's Method 2
                for j in range(done_i + 1, min(n, done_i + 40)):
                    back = c[j - off] if j - off >= 0 else None
                    if back is None:
                        continue
                    if (c[j] < back) if up else (c[j] > back):
                        fire = j
                        break
            else:                                 # Countdown to 13
                k = 0
                for j in range(done_i + 1, n):
                    if j - cdo < 0:
                        continue
                    if (c[j] >= h[j - cdo]) if up else (c[j] <= l[j - cdo]):
                        k += 1
                        if k >= cdl:
                            fire = j
                            break
            if fire is not None and not sig[fire]:
                sig[fire] = d
                lvl[fire] = ext
    ctx.sig = ctx.series(sig, "tdsig")
    ctx.tdst = ctx.series(lvl, "tdst")
    ctx._lv = None
    ctx._lvd = 0


def signal(ctx, i):
    s = ctx.sig[i]
    if not s:
        return 0
    v = ctx.tdst[i]
    if v is not None:
        ctx._lv = v
        ctx._lvd = 1 if s > 0 else -1
    return 1 if s > 0 else -1


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    if ctx._lv is None or not ctx._dir or ctx._lvd != ctx._dir:
        return False
    if ctx._dir > 0:
        return ctx.c[i] > ctx._lv
    return ctx.c[i] < ctx._lv
